summary:
# FIRE FUSION — When Space Meets Earth

FIRE FUSION, developed by Global Synthetic Squad (G.S.S.), is a wildfire monitoring and early-warning prototype concept that connects space-based observations with ground-level environmental monitoring.

The project combines NASA LANCE FIRMS active-fire observations, including MODIS and VIIRS data, with SYLVAN SPHERE 1.0, a conceptual ground-based IoT monitoring system featuring environmental sensing, gas detection, thermal monitoring, and a proposed Microbial Fuel Cell (MFC) energy system.

FIRE FUSION addresses fragmented wildfire information through a seven-stage data harmonization pipeline: ingestion, normalization, filtering, matching, clustering, scoring, and visualization. By organizing satellite observations and exploring their correlation with ground telemetry through a proposed LoRaWAN communication architecture, the system aims to improve fire-event assessment, reduce false alarms, and provide unified wildfire intelligence through a monitoring dashboard.

Wildfires threaten forests, biodiversity, wildlife, and communities worldwide. FIRE FUSION envisions shifting wildfire management from reactive response toward proactive protection by supporting earlier awareness, better-informed decisions, and more connected environmental monitoring.

**FIRE FUSION — From Detection to Protection.**

FIRE FUSION — When Space Meets Earth

Global Synthetic Squad (G.S.S.)

Project Description

FIRE FUSION is an innovative wildfire monitoring and intelligence project developed by Global Synthetic Squad (G.S.S.). It connects space-based fire observations with ground-level environmental monitoring through a unified data harmonization and visualization framework.

What We Developed

FIRE FUSION integrates NASA LANCE FIRMS active-fire observations from MODIS and VIIRS satellite instruments, leveraging satellite-derived thermal anomaly information for wildfire monitoring. MODIS data plays an important role in our satellite observation layer, providing fire detection information that supports the identification, analysis, and organization of potential wildfire events.

The project also incorporates SYLVAN SPHERE 1.0, our ground-monitoring concept, designed around environmental sensing, gas detection, thermal infrared monitoring, and a Microbial Fuel Cell (MFC)-based sustainable energy architecture.

How It Works

FIRE FUSION follows a seven-stage data harmonization pipeline:

Ingestion → Normalization → Filtering → Matching → Clustering → Scoring → Visualization

The pipeline processes satellite observations, including MODIS and VIIRS fire detections, standardizes relevant information, filters observations, identifies relationships, groups detections into potential fire events, evaluates relevant indicators, and presents organized wildfire intelligence through a monitoring dashboard.

The space-to-ground architecture connects satellite observations with environmental monitoring data. SYLVAN SPHERE 1.0 incorporates a proposed LoRaWAN-based communication architecture for transmitting ground-level environmental telemetry.

Innovation and Impact

FIRE FUSION introduces a space-to-ground wildfire intelligence framework combining NASA MODIS and VIIRS observations, data harmonization, environmental monitoring, and visualization within a unified wildfire monitoring approach.

By organizing satellite-derived fire information and exploring its correlation with ground-level environmental observations, FIRE FUSION aims to improve wildfire situational awareness, support fire-event assessment, and reduce potential false alarms.

Wildfires threaten forests, wildlife, biodiversity, and human communities. FIRE FUSION envisions a future where connected satellite intelligence and ground-level monitoring support earlier wildfire awareness, better-informed decisions, and proactive environmental protection.

Technology and Development

Our project incorporates NASA LANCE FIRMS, MODIS and VIIRS fire observations, data harmonization methodologies, monitoring dashboard development, and the SYLVAN SPHERE 1.0 ground-monitoring architecture.

Our team utilized AI-assisted research, coding support, documentation, visual design, and video-production tools, including ChatGPT, Gemini, Canva, Google Flow, Google AI Studio, CapCut, and ElevenLabs.
